deviations: RED used the charter's second menu option (in-vitro close/listen over the real serveWithChatProxy/stopServer code with a real open connection) rather than a watchdog firing on the reproduced stall, because the live web-only orchestration completed pre-fix and the full orchestrated stall additionally requires ORI-AI-002's write-prohibited caller adapter; recorded explicitly in .tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-004-2/red.json.

A web-leg error (including a StallError) now converts to a failed LegOutcome with a manifest write and CLI exit 1, where pre-fix it propagated as an uncaught throw with exit 2 and no manifest — the exported surface, flags, and schemas are untouched, but the error-to-exit mapping changed deliberately so stalls are recorded rather than crash-losing the manifest.

The driver gained additive exports the charter did not name (serveWithChatProxy, stopServer, BackendSession, StallError, heartbeatRecords, HeartbeatEntry) so the harness can exercise the real lifecycle code; the consumed runLiveExampleProof/options.backend seam is byte-compatible in behavior.

The harness performs one real mid-stream client abort directly against the owned backend so the run's correlation carries an aborted record, because the web leg alone cannot produce one (see findings).
concerns: The pipeline-tail bound on a caller adapter's stop is proven by construction and by the bounded-wait machinery, not by a live adapter hang — ORI-AI-002's cycle 3 is the first execution of the real six-target matrix against that bound, so its first stalled-or-passed result is the true confirmation.

The Android stop-turn timing remains historically sensitive (maestro ceremony vs a 4096-token essay); tonight's matrix passed both appearances, but a slow machine can still race the stop tap — the per-turn record gates will fail loudly rather than hang if it does.

The leg-budget timer cannot fire during the native legs' long synchronous spawnSync sections; it is a backstop at await points only, so a sync-blocked native leg still relies on the outer runner watchdog (documented in the harness header).

evidence/ORI-RN-004/heartbeat.log is append-only across runs; consumers must filter by the run field, and a long-lived checkout accumulates entries (cosmetic, but a naive line count across runs would be wrong).

Two development runs died to unhandled ECONNRESET on sockets whose error handlers had been removed/never attached, and each crash orphaned the backend child on port 4000 so the next run failed with 'port 4000 already in use' — any runner holding raw sockets to the backend or proxy must attach error handlers and clean port 4000 before relaunching.
findings: The web proxy does NOT propagate client aborts upstream: when the browser aborts a fetch (the Stop control), the proxy's undici fetch keeps the upstream connection open and the backend generation runs to natural completion, so a web-leg stop turn produces a delayed 'completed' record and never an 'aborted' one — ORI-AI-002's validator must not expect an aborted record from the uniwind web leg (native legs produce them because the app connects directly; my harness injects one real direct-backend abort to satisfy the correlation shape).

A web-only runLiveExampleProof invocation records manifest passed_platforms: 1 and completed: false because completed literally means 3 platforms — pre-existing semantics I deliberately left untouched, so ORI-AI-002's per-phase validation must key on legs[].status, not manifest.completed, for single-platform invocations.

Node's closeIdleConnections is more aggressive than the charter assumed: it destroys sockets with a received-but-unresponded request (an incomplete-body POST and even a not-yet-first-chunk proxied SSE both count as idle); only connections with an in-flight, headers-written response survive the sweep, which is exactly what the 20s bound plus closeAllConnections covers.

Driver teardown ownership rule: with options.backend set and the driver having restarted it, the driver stops only ITS restart child (session.current), never the caller's initial handle — ORI-AI-002's owner process must stop its own initial handle at phase teardown or it lingers on port 4000.

New observability for the runner: every driver invocation appends run-scoped JSON lines to tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-RN-004/heartbeat.log and prints '[heartbeat <ts>] step' lines to stderr; entries carry run = runId, so the runner can assert per-phase coverage/ordering and read the last heartbeat out of stall diagnostics (StallError messages embed step, port, boundMs, and lastHeartbeat).

The manifest's commands field is hardcoded to the three-platform CLI string even when the driver is invoked through the export with a caller backend and a different platform subset, so export-driven single-platform runs carry a stale-looking commands entry — harmless to the frozen schema but a staleness validator keying on commands would misfire.

The caller handle's launch options pass through unmodified (options.backend is consumed as-is), and a higher maxOutputTokens widens the Stop-control window — my harness used 16384 versus the driver's self-launched 4096 and both worked.

Matrix runtime expectations: the full three-platform run took roughly 25-30 minutes wall-clock (ios and android legs dominate; the web leg is only ~2-4 minutes), and expo export completed in ~10-20 seconds warm thanks to expo's persistent transform cache, producing a 6.0MB dist under os.tmpdir() — which under cmux agent shells IS the reaper's agent-scratch directory, so the documented reaper sweeps remain a live risk for a 1.5-2h six-target run.

The reserved-device env vars were not exported in the implementer environment; the reserved iOS simulator is RNR_S05_IOS_UDID=81487B1E-A4D1-45AE-9BCE-D675802BACD1 (iPhone 17, iOS 26.3, derived from FIX-ORI-RN-003-2 session evidence) with RNR_S05_ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554, both required for any native-including run while web-only runs skip reserveDevices entirely.
feedback: The AC-1 RED menu's 'in-vitro real open connection' underspecifies what reliably blocks server.close(): a streaming essay as the held connection degenerates when the model finishes (~25s) and the close resolves naturally, producing a weak red — name the deterministic blocker (an incomplete-body POST plus an in-flight SSE response, which is what survives the idle sweep) so the next implementer does not burn a cycle discovering it.

AC-2's 'completed == true for the platforms run' is ambiguous against the driver's literal manifest.completed (=== 3 platforms): state explicitly that single-platform invocations legitimately record completed:false and that the assertion keys on legs[].status, or explicitly authorize changing the semantics.

Record the reserved-device values (or their canonical evidence source) in the task's fixture block — both RNR_S05_IOS_UDID and RNR_S05_ANDROID_SERIAL were unset in the environment and had to be derived from a sibling task's evidence.

The command-contract note about direct pnpm-wrapped biome invocations dying with exit 254 in shimmed shells was accurate and saved real time; keep that pattern, and consider naming the clean-env invocation shape that works (env -i with explicit pnpm/node PATH).
